findings.evidence: "Rank the primary user tasks and list the content that must appear in every alternative" and "Ask which to pick" largely activate familiar UX and conversation practices. Much of the workflow specifies standard activities rather than transferring expert-only ASCII layout knowledge.
findings.fix: Condense routine elicitation and selection instructions, and add concrete ASCII layout constraints: derive minimum column widths from required labels, preserve shared column positions when truncating comparison values, and define when insufficient width requires moving secondary fields into a detail view.

findings.evidence: "Classify the dominant task (compare records, inspect one item, complete a sequence), then vary one structural axis per alternative" supplies a useful framework but leaves the connection between task classification and structural choice implicit.
findings.fix: Add a short decision rule connecting task to structure: comparisons favor persistent aligned fields; inspection favors master/detail when both panes remain readable, otherwise a single detail view; sequences favor a wizard when later steps depend on earlier answers, otherwise a single-page form. Generate alternatives around those constraints rather than varying axes without a selection rule.
